core: Keep exactly the parent q momentum box and energy radius. Any candidate flat-band double eigenvalue in its momentum projection first receives a Weyl energy window, then a weighted Schur trace bound. Require that entire candidate-energy bound to fit strictly inside the parent energy radius. Combine this with parent existence/uniqueness and endpoint joins. weighted_schur: At the fixed parent midpoint frame F and complement Q, K0=Q.T H0 Q-E0 I. Use R=abs(K0)^(-1/2). Retain Gram blocks B_i.T abs(K0)^(-1) B_j for B0, B_f1, B_f2 and B_Dpredictor. A Weyl bound |E-Ebar|<=W and matrix bound L give eta=(L+W)/G0. For eta<1, ||B.T K^-1 B|| <= ||R B||^2/(1-eta). Bound ||R B|| by its maximum at the eight vertices of each affine cell, with a fixed norm allowance.
exclusion: Outside the unchanged core, compute the exact minimum Euclidean norm of the projected traceless affine residual on the momentum rectangle by its four edges or an interior zero, and subtract the bounded D variation and energy allowance. A lower residual exceeding the weighted Schur correction plus the frozen margin excludes any flat-band double eigenvalue in that entire cell and its full candidate-energy window.

Test every cell; bisect failed cells along their largest width times the inherited Hamiltonian derivative norm. Retain all attempts, parent/child indices and unresolved leaves.
